page: The UpCloud PREMIUM-32xCPU-64GB is a KVM-based virtual server featuring 32 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz with 32 physical cores and a single thread per core configuration under a shared allocation model. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 400 GB SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong compute capabilities. The AMD EPYC processor achieves top-tier performance in stress-ng single-core CPU tests and strong performance in multi-core execution. Cryptographic and compression workloads perform well, with bzip3 single-threaded decompression reaching top-tier speeds and gzip compression scoring in the top 25%. Memory read bandwidth is strong at 230.25 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, though write bandwidth and PassMark memory scores are relatively weaker, placing in the average and bottom quartiles respectively.

From a resource allocation perspective, the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio positions this instance as a compute-heavy option. The shared CPU allocation model introduces potential performance variability compared to dedicated core instances, which represents a key tradeoff for sustained high-load operations. However, the inclusion of a 400 GB SSD and high multi-core benchmark efficiency provides a cost-effective density of processing power for workloads that do not require massive memory footprints.

This server configuration is suited for multi-threaded processing tasks, web serving, and database operations, as evidenced by its strong PassMark database and Redis SET performance. It is also capable of handling light LLM inference tasks, such as prompt processing and text generation for smaller models, as well as parallel compilation and general-purpose compute workloads.
description: The UpCloud PREMIUM-32xCPU-64GB is a KVM-based virtual server featuring 32 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz. It is configured with 64.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core) and a bundled 400 GB SSD. Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core CPU performance and strong multi-core execution, alongside high memory read bandwidth. However, memory write speeds and PassMark memory scores represent a relative bottleneck, performing in the average and lower quartiles. With its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server offers a compute-dense profile. It is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, database operations, static web serving, and moderate parallel processing tasks that require high CPU capacity without requiring massive memory allocations.
